title: UDLM Regeneration Manifest (the durable change record of a class change)
description: Machine-validatable regeneration manifest — the durable change record a registry class change emits. Shared building blocks are the point of the class system and also its risk: one Base element serves dozens of descendants, so changing it changes every artifact compiled from it, and every downstream consumer still reading an earlier revision starts carrying version debt. ADR-045 Decision 2 rules that the resulting ripple is computed from the class graph and never hand-listed; this record is where that computation lands so it can be read, reviewed, and audited long after the merge. It names the artifact that changed, how the compatibility classifier ruled and by which rule, the full affected set (each artifact by handle, version, and digest, with what happened to it), the consumers now accruing debt (read from the ADR-044 manifests in registry/consumers/), the standing gate suite that re-proved the regenerated set, and the registry ref the whole change landed under — which is also the only pin an estate can take inside the registry (ADR-045 Decision 3). The per-entity commit log (commit-log-entry.schema.json) cannot carry this: it records one entity's mutation and a fingerprint, whereas a class change is one decision over a computed set of artifacts. In the surface/decide/enable division of labour (docs/design/operational-response-matrix.md), this record is the SURFACE half of the Base/Type class-change row — the platform states the blast radius; the organization's own change policy decides what to do about it.

record_type.description: Dispatch discriminator (data-model-core §2); registry/tools/validate.py routes on it.

uuid.description: RFC 9562 v4 identity of this manifest. A manifest is a point-in-time fact about one change set — it is never edited; a correction is a new manifest (its own uuid) that names this one in `supersedes` (the ADR-051 immutable-record family).

supersedes.description: OPTIONAL — the uuid of the manifest this record replaces (ADR-051 family rule: an immutable record changes by publishing a NEW record that names its predecessor; the identity-integrity gate refuses in-place edits). The superseded record's bytes remain in the revision store.

handle.description: Advisory human identity, e.g. regeneration/2026-07-25/compute-base-scope-narrowing. The uuid is authoritative.

version.description: OPTIONAL — this record's own version. Manifests are normally minted once and left alone; a version appears only where a producer versions the manifest shape it emits.

title.description: One line a reviewer can read cold: what changed and how it was classified.

registry_ref.description: The registry revision this change set landed as. The registry ref pins everything at once and is the sole intra-registry pinning mechanism (ADR-045 Decision 3), so it is the coordinate an estate uses to place this change relative to its own pins.

commit.description: The commit the change set landed as — full 40-hex preferred; an abbreviated ref is accepted for readability.

branch.description: OPTIONAL — the branch or release line the commit landed on.

released_as.description: OPTIONAL — the release tag or name this ref was published under, where the registry publishes releases.

change.description: The change that started the ripple — the one artifact a maintainer actually edited. Everything in affected_artifacts is downstream of this.

artifact.description: The changed artifact at its NEW revision.

previous.description: The same artifact at its prior revision. Absent only when the artifact is newly introduced (nothing was replaced).

summary.description: What changed, in ordinary sentences — the element added, removed, reshaped, or moved between scopes. The classifier's verdict lives in `classification`; this says what a human would say at a whiteboard.

classification.description: How the compatibility classifier ruled on the change, and by which rule. Classification is by rule, never by review judgment (ADR-045 Decision 4) — which is why the rule that produced the verdict is recorded alongside the verdict itself.

compatibility.description: additive = the surface only grew, existing carriers keep validating; breaking = an existing carrier stops validating or loses portable surface (includes element removal and any move to a narrower scope, which no schema differ can see); revision = neither — descriptions, prose, and other content changes with no surface effect.

classified_by.description: The classifier rule that produced the verdict, named as it appears in the classifier's own rule table (e.g. the element-scope-narrowing rule of ADR-045 Decision 4, or the field-removal row of VERSIONING.md). Once the class-compat rule family is registered in registry/rule-id-registry.yaml this carries the rule ID.

declared_bump.description: The bump the change actually declared on the changed artifact.

enforced_bump.description: OPTIONAL — the bar the gate enforced, where it differs from required_bump. Pre-1.0 a breaking change is permitted under a MINOR bump (VERSIONING.md, the pre-1.0 bump floor); the classification stays visible either way, which is the point of recording both.

reasons.description: The individual findings behind the verdict — one entry per difference the classifier saw. Populated by the classifier; a breaking verdict with no reason is a defect in the emitter, not a terse manifest.

level.description: The bump this single difference on its own would demand.

detail.description: The difference in concrete terms — the element or field, and what happened to it.

affected_artifacts.description: The blast radius: every artifact the class graph says this change reached, each pinned to a revision. Computed by the enumerator from the class graph — a hand-assembled list defeats the record's only purpose. An empty array is legal and meaningful (a leaf class with no descendants) but it is still an assertion the enumerator makes, not an omission.

artifact.description: The affected artifact at its revision AFTER the change set.

previous.description: The same artifact before the change set. Absent where the artifact is new.

disposition.description: What the atomic recompilation did to it (ADR-045 Decision 1, on the ADR-051 model). regenerated = a generated flat spec re-rendered from the class graph; revalidated_bumped = an authored Type or Provider Class whose own content changed, so it bumped its version under the publish law (identity uuid frozen; a new digest row lands in the pin manifest); revalidated_unchanged = an authored artifact that re-validated with no content change and therefore did NOT bump — the identity gate's no-op rule.

path.description: OPTIONAL — the repository-relative path of the artifact, for reviewers reading the manifest next to the diff.

reached_via.description: OPTIONAL — the class-graph path from the changed artifact to this one (each hop by handle). This is what makes the set auditable rather than merely asserted: a reader can re-walk the reason each artifact is in the list.

consumer_debt.description: The downstream consumers this change puts into version debt, derived from the consumer manifests in registry/consumers/ (ADR-044 — consumers declare what they read). Debt is legal and expected: an organization pinned behind is exercising control, and the platform's obligation is that the distance is never silent (ADR-045 Decision 3). An empty array means the enumerator found no consumer reading the affected surface — again an assertion, not an omission.

consumer.description: The consumer's declared name, as it appears in its manifest.

manifest_ref.description: Repository-relative path of the consumer manifest this entry was read from — the evidence for the claim.

handle.description: The affected artifact the consumer reads (a type handle such as Compute.VM, or a class handle).

noted_version.description: The version the consumer declared it reads. Absent for a manifest that declares whole-tree consumption without naming versions.

registry_version.description: The version the registry now carries for that artifact after this change set.

debt.description: behind = legal, enumerated debt — the consumer reads an older revision and re-opens the question when it advances its registry ref; current = no distance; ahead and unknown_revision are refusals, not debt (ADR-045 Decision 3), and appear here only to name a consumer whose declaration cannot resolve; version_undeclared = the manifest consumes the tree without naming versions, so distance is not computable from it.

distance.description: OPTIONAL — the distance in the terms the consumer gate reports it (e.g. 'one minor behind'). Derived; recorded for readability, never as an independent fact.

gate_suite.description: The standing gate suite that re-proved the regenerated set. Atomic recompilation means the existing deterministic hammer suite runs against every regenerated artifact in the same change (ADR-045 Consequences) — so this block names gates that already exist and always run, never tests authored for this one change. Its presence is what turns 'the change was verified' from an assertion into a citation.

runner.description: The authority that ran the suite — the CI workflow or validation runner, not the person who proposed the change. Same attribution discipline the DecisionRecord applies to validation evidence.

gate.description: The gate as it runs — its script path or CI job name, so a reader can run it themselves.

result.description: A manifest recording a failed or skipped gate is a legitimate record of a change that did not earn its merge; the emitter never silently drops a gate.

covered.description: OPTIONAL — how many artifacts of the affected set this gate actually examined.

evidence_ref.description: OPTIONAL — where the run's output can be retrieved (job reference, attestation artifact).

decision_refs.description: OPTIONAL — the DecisionRecords or ADRs that authorized or motivated the change (by uuid or handle). The manifest records what happened; the decision record records why.

emitted_at.description: When the manifest was emitted, RFC 3339 UTC 'Z' (common-elements §8).

provenance.description: What produced this manifest. REQUIRED because the record's authority rests entirely on being computed: a manifest with no named enumerator is a hand-written list wearing a schema.

enumerator.description: The blast-radius enumerator that produced the affected set — tool name or path.

enumerator_version.description: The enumerator's version, so an old manifest can be read against the logic that produced it.

artifact_revision.description: One artifact at one exact revision. A published (identity, version) is immutable and its content digest names the exact bytes (ADR-051; VERSIONING.md § "Identity, version, digest") — so handle plus version plus digest names a thing, a claim about it, and the exact bytes that claim is about. The digest lives HERE, in the referrer, never in the artifact itself.

artifact_kind.description: Which layer of the model the artifact belongs to. The three class scopes are Base/Type/Provider (ADR-038); generated_type_spec is the flat spec compiled from them; provider_definition and capability are the provider-edge units that version under the same rules (ADR-045 §8).

handle.description: The artifact's stable name — the thing that persists across revisions.

digest.description: sha256 over the revision's RFC 8785-canonical form (the pin manifest's recorded value) — the exact-bytes half of the ADR-051 pin grammar.
